findings.claim: PARTIAL closure: the expanded matrix still cannot establish the promised predicate-by-predicate, target-only mutation evidence. Several prescribed mutants cannot change their target result, some fixtures do not isolate K2b, and independent H2/parser predicates remain without dedicated counterexamples. Acceptance 4 nevertheless requires every listed pair to kill, so an executor must change the frozen acceptance or manufacture credit.

observed: The table has exactly 72 distinct row IDs. R01 assigns the nonempty-value mutant to both a wrong nonempty string and an empty string; on the empty target, both exact equality and bool(value) are false. Line 218 requires a separate mutant/target for each counterexample, so the empty target cannot kill that prescribed mutant.

R07 assigns ordinary JSON decoding to both duplicate keys and non-JSON. json.loads("not JSON") raises JSONDecodeError, so that mutation still rejects the malformed target. R09 assigns str(value) to a singleton-list target; str(["cho-phep-bo-moi-pr3"]) is not "cho-phep-bo-moi-pr3", so the mutant still refuses. R10 changes only the variable read: the bo_moi value still differs from the che_do_dich permit string. A mutation of the complete variable/permit pair would be distinguishable, but is not what the row specifies.

Literal G05/G06 additions to DC-du leave the correct run 100 and all eight successful full-G5 shards intact. The actual current CLI remains rc=0 and the selected evidence still satisfies the stated du conditions. Unlike G04, these rows do not say to make the correct run incomplete; their required K2b-red baseline is therefore underspecified.

For D02/D04 with an M9-touching diff, the current real CLI returns rc=12 at K7 alone when the audit is absent or has the wrong H. With a docs-only diff it returns rc=0. Thus the promised all-other-K0-K7-green counterexamples require an explicit outside-M9 fixture or suitable waiver; DC-delta does not specify that prerequisite, and D02 explicitly forbids a waiver.

Residual independent coverage holes include malformed members/non-string names inside an otherwise present steps list (G11 only removes steps), duplicate or in-progress target-mode steps (G12/G14 cover only S_DU), and duplicate/unknown optional cong_cu or g5_che_do output values (T07/T08 exercise only che_do). The common ChotB4 contract is now stated, but the new matrix is not yet a complete executable proof of every new guard.

findings.suggested_fix: Revise the matrix as one acceptance correction. Give the empty-value and malformed-JSON targets their own distinguishing faults; replace the equivalent singleton-list str() mutant with an explicitly faulty scalar extraction/acceptance mutation; specify whether R10 mutates the whole class-to-variable/permit mapping. Make G05/G06 retain valid K2 evidence while removing full-G5 evidence from the correct run. Define the M9/waiver preconditions for each D target so K7 remains green. Add the missing independent H2/parser cases and mutants. Require a healthy control plus each target result under the correct and mutated consumer, with ChotB4 credit attributed to that exact target; setup failures, ordinary AssertionError, crashes and timeouts remain false credit. Do not weaken production guards or borrow a different failing case to make the inventory pass.

findings.claim: The classifier output contract lacks a compatible Windows line-framing rule. H1 rejects a trailing CR and T08 requires that rejection, but the unchanged classifier only sets stdout encoding/errors, leaving Windows newline translation active. Ordinary Windows CRLF output is consequently indistinguishable from the rejected T08 bytes unless the runner explicitly guarantees LF. This can leave the designated Windows switch-reading host unable to classify either alpha or beta even after its REST capability is proven.

evidence.observed: The actual origin/master classifier _ep_utf8 at lines 145-148 calls reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="backslashreplace") without newline. Running its actual main through a TextIOWrapper configured for Windows CRLF produced rc=0 and b"che_do=day_du\r" before the LF; the exact H1 value check is false. The ordinary Linux replay passes all 60 classifications. This is a Linux simulation of Windows stream translation, not a native Windows run; the conflict is between the required bytes and the current producer, not a claim that Windows was measured.

findings.suggested_fix: Freeze an explicit line-framing contract for the trusted runner. Prefer making the child emit LF before executing the unchanged master blob, within B4's allowed runner, and preserve strict value matching. Alternatively define precisely which CRLF framing is accepted and revise T08 so it still detects a CR in the value. Add a real-producer transport regression with LF and Windows-style CRLF, plus a malformed-value control; keep the separately authorized native Windows qualification before beta use. Do not silently strip arbitrary whitespace or edit the out-of-scope classifier.

findings.claim: The planned sensitive packet exceeds its applicable file-count cap without a size declaration or exception. No ADR-0053 activation line is present, so the applicable fallback is three files / 300 added lines. The two product/test files, mandatory runbook and mandatory committed replay script already require at least four distinct delivery files, even before the spec, A/B scripts or evidence. r85's call/CI budgets do not override this size limit.

evidence.observed: activation_lines=[]; nang_tran_present=false; minimum distinct required delivery files=4. ADR-0053 explicitly retains the old 3-file/300-added-line cap when its activation declaration is absent. Its valid land anchor 8ab100793df9831505f495543a74044b91c2c9ab was verified: ADR exists there (rc=0), is absent at its first parent (rc=128), and L is on current master's first-parent chain. Implementation numstat is not measured because there is no implementation yet.

findings.suggested_fix: Before freezing, specify the delivery file inventory, activate ADR-0053 with its verified OID if adopting the six-file/450-added-line cap, and estimate the complete code/test/runbook/measurement scope. If the chosen cap is insufficient, include an owner-approved nang_tran with ai_nang, can_cu, tran_cu and tran_moi, carried into the installing Mission revision and lease. Require actual numstat before each source review and a stop on overflow. Keep all acceptance cases; do not compress or omit evidence just to fit an unstated budget.

findings.claim: Section 6b scopes _rest_get to all network I/O of packet_loop.py, contradicting both the unchanged-command boundary and the required Git transport. Existing K0 uses git ls-remote, other commands fetch/read remote refs, and new self-check 7a itself requires git ls-remote. Those operations cannot all go through the specified urllib GET/status/headers/body function without changing unrelated behavior.

evidence.observed: Current _git_do at line 2508 invokes Git subprocesses; record-lease fetches at line 2702, accept reads remote refs at line 3067, and kiem-merge K0 calls ls-remote at line 3565. SPEC line 75 says all network I/O of packet_loop.py goes through _rest_get, while lines 20 and 86 respectively preserve existing behavior and explicitly require Git ls-remote.

findings.suggested_fix: Narrow line 75 to all new REST I/O for B4 switch reads. Explicitly preserve existing Git and lifecycle transports and keep their A/B obligations. This is a wording correction, not authorization to refactor other commands or move Git requests into urllib.
